auth.title: OAuth
auth.snippet:
## OAuth Authentication
OAuth users need to register an app with us before using this feature. Visit our [OAuth Setup Guide](/oauth) to get your client credentials and configure your redirect URL.
Both TypeScript and Python SDKs support OAuth 2.0 authentication for building integrations that can be installed by multiple Fathom accounts.
---
### Step 1: Get Authorization URL
Using the `Client ID` and `Client Secret` you received when registering your app, generate an authorization URL that users will visit to grant your app access:
### Step 2: Handle OAuth Callback
After the user authorizes your app, they’ll be redirected back to your redirect URI with an authorization code. Use this code to exchange it for access tokens:
```
import { Fathom } from 'fathom-typescript';
// User gets redirected here with code
const tokenStore = Fathom.newTokenStore();  // demo only — use persistent store in production
const fathom = new Fathom({
security: Fathom.withAuthorization({
clientId: "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
clientSecret: "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
code: "AUTHORIZATION_CODE_FROM_CALLBACK",
redirectUri: "https://your_redirect_url",
tokenStore
}),
});
// Now you can make requests and the SDK will refresh tokens as needed
const result = await fathom.listMeetings({});
```
newTokenStore() is an in-memory store — great for demos and quick starts. For production, you’ll want a persistent TokenStore so users only need to install once.
### Step 3: Token Management & Persistence
For production, you’ll want to implement your own `TokenStore` that persists tokens to a database, cache, or file. The SDK will automatically call your `set()` when new tokens are issued, and `get()` when it needs to reuse or refresh them.

**Usage:**
```
token_store = SQLiteTokenStore()
fathom = Fathom(security=Fathom.with_authorization(
client_id,
client_secret,
authorization_code,
redirect_uri,
token_store
))
```

**Exchange authorization code for tokens:**
```
curl -X POST https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1/oauth2/token \
-H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
-d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
-d "code=AUTH_CODE" \
-d "client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID" \
-d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
-d "redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI"
```
This returns a JSON object with both an `access_token` and a `refresh_token`. **Refresh an expired access token:**
```
curl -X POST https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1/oauth2/token \
-H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
-d "grant_type=refresh_token" \
-d "r

auth.title: Basic Usage
auth.snippet:
## Authentication
Authentication tokens are required for API requests.
The SDK performs the obtaining of tokens for the user when creating a Client object. Just use the access credentials supplied by Fathom.
```
from fathom.sdk.v2 import Client
client = Client(
"client_id",
"client_secret",
)
# Future requests will be authenticated
```
To access data from the REST API endpoints you will need to authorize requests using a JWT token in the `Authorization` header. To be able to do this, you must obtain a token from our authorization server using your supplied `client_id` and `client_secret`.
```
curl --request POST \
--url https://api.fathom.global/v2/auth/token \
--header 'content-type: application/json' \
--data '{"client_id":"CLIENT_ID","client_secret":"CLIENT_SECRET"}'
```
You should obtain a response like:
```
{
"access_token": "access_token",
"expire_secs": 86400
}
```
When you have the Auth0 JWT token you will need to pass it as a header with every request to any of the Fathom API endpoints using the pattern:
```
Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN
```

auth.title: Authentication · Fathom Analytics API
auth.snippet:
# Authentication
To connect to our API, you must use the `Authorization` header with a bearer token. This can be obtained from your dashboard, under Settings → API. Your API key has complete access to your account (depending on the permissions you set), so please protect it.
You should also send `Accept: application/json` so that errors are returned as JSON.
```
curl "https://api.usefathom.com/v1/account" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
-H "Accept: application/json"
```

auth.title: Api overview
auth.snippet:
This documentation describes Fathom’s REST API.
## Authentication
All REST API resources are authenticated with API keys generated via the Fathom website’s settings area.
## Rate limiting
We use several rate limiting strategies to ensure the availability of our APIs. Rate-limited calls to our APIs return a 429 status code. Calls to our APIs include headers indicating the current rate limit status.
### Global rate limits
Authenticated requests are subject to a global limit. This is the maximum number of calls that your account can make to the API per minute. Endpoints subject to rate limits may return the headers below.
| Header | Description |
|---|---|
| `RateLimit-Limit` | The maximum number of requests allowed in a time window |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | The number of requests remaining in the current time window |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | The time remaining in the current time window |
| `Retry-After` | The number of seconds to wait before retrying. Only sent on 429 responses |
Currently, you are able to make a maximum of 60 calls to the API in a 60 second window. The official SDKs automatically retry rate-limited requests, waiting for the duration indicated by the `Retry-After` header. If you are calling the API directly, wait at least `Retry-After` seconds before retrying a 429 response.

### OAuth Rate Limits
60 requests per 60 seconds per OAuth app for the `https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1/oauth2/token` endpoint

### Does my plan include API access?
Yes. API access—keys and webhooks— are included on all plans. Generate a key in User Settings → API Access.

access.title: Pick Your API Limits - Fathom Analytics
access.snippet:
Every Fathom account comes with free API access, and that isn’t changing. But some of you push the API hard: polling dashboards every few seconds, running nightly exports across dozens of sites, building custom reports for clients. One flat limit was never going to suit everyone.
So we’ve added API plans. Pick the plan that matches how hard you use the API and your limits go up right away. A paid plan raises both of our API limits:
- **Requests per hour** across every endpoint, so you can make more calls over the course of an hour.
- **Concurrent requests** across every endpoint, so you can run more at the same time.
Plans start at $19/mo and go up to $399/mo for heavy volume, which gets you 16,000 requests an hour and 25 running at once. Pay yearly and you get two months free, just like your main plan.
It’s all self-serve. Open your billing settings, hit Change Plan, and choose your tier. The new limits apply immediately, and you can move up or down whenever your usage shifts.

access.title: Public API
access.snippet:
Fathom now has a public API that gives you developer‑friendly access to meeting insights so you can build workflows and integrations that connect Fathom with the rest of your tools.

- Partners can register an OAuth app to be eligible for a future marketplace listing as a Fathom‑approved integration.

### Keep in mind
- **API keys and access**: API keys are created at the user level. Your key can access meetings recorded by you or shared to your Team. Admin API keys do not grant access to other users’ unshared meetings.
- **Rate Limiting**: users can make 60 calls per minute across all of their API keys; this ensures system stability and reliability. With that in mind, we do not offer higher rate limits at this time.

access.title: Fathom API Review: Endpoints, SDKs & Rate Limits [Aug 2026]
access.snippet:
The [Fathom Developer Hub](https://developers.fathom.ai/) documents a REST surface at https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1/, with TypeScript and Python SDKs, OAuth 2.0 for public integrations, webhook support, and an [MCP server](https://developers.fathom.ai/mcp-docs) for AI assistants. API access is available on [all plan tiers](https://fathom.ai/pricing) including the free plan, which is uncommon for a meeting intelligence platform. The developer docs are public, the OpenAPI spec is downloadable, and you can generate an API key and start making calls without upgrading.

| **Rate limits** | 60 requests per [60-second window](https://developers.fathom.ai/api-overview#rate-limiting) (global); 30 per 60 seconds for heavy endpoints |

| **Pricing / access** | Included on [all plans including free](https://fathom.ai/pricing); no per-call or per-credit charges |

API access starts immediately on any **Fathom** plan, including the free tier. There is no developer approval process, no separate API subscription, and no enterprise gate. You generate an API key from the API Access section of your Settings page and start making calls.
[API keys are user-scoped](https://developers.fathom.ai/quickstart#generate-an-api-key): a key can only access meetings recorded by the key-holder or shared with their team.

**Fathom** takes the simplest approach to API pricing: access is included on [all plan tiers](https://fathom.ai/pricing), including the free plan, with no per-call charges, no credit system, and no metered pricing.
What each plan tier means for API access:
- **Free ($0):** API key generation and full endpoint access. Basic summaries in API responses. CRM match data (contacts, companies, deals) is not available.
- **Team ($15/user/month annual, $19/month monthly, 2-user minimum):** Unlimited AI features, public API access, and SSO. CRM syncs are still limited to 3 users per domain.
- **Business ($25/user/month annual, $34/month monthly, 2-user minimum):** CRM field sync with unlimited users, which means CRM match data (contacts, deals, companies in crm_matches) appears in API responses. Custom data retention policies.
The practical cost constraint is not the API but the features behind the data. If your integration needs CRM-matched contact and deal information in the meeting payload, you need a Business plan. If you only need transcripts, summaries, and action items, the free plan or Team plan covers it.
No enterprise or custom API pricing tier is published. No overag

mcp.title: Connect to Fathom's MCP server
mcp.snippet:
# What is an MCP server?
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides your AI tool with access to your Fathom data and the **context the tool needs to understand the data**.
By connecting Fathom’s MCP server, your AI tool has the logic behind how the data relates to one another, not just the hard-coded numbers. MCP servers help AI tools, like large-language models (LLMs), understand your data when you ask a natural language question, so the tool can retrieve and reference the correct data.
## What can you do with Fathom's MCP server?
With Fathom’s MCP server, you can use natural language to interrogate and analyse your Fathom data in your chosen AI tool (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, etc.).
📝 **Note:** We've heard from users that the "free version" of Claude does not allow you to use PAT tokens to connect to MCPs, including Fathom's MCP server.
​You can bring your Fathom data into your connected AI tool, but you cannot send instructions or data back into Fathom.
| Fathom's MCP server will provide the connected AI tool with the following types of data: |
|---|
| - The Fathom organisations or accounts you are a member of ​ - The companies connected to your Fathom organisation(s) that you can access ​ - P&L data for your entities ​ - Balance Sheet data for your entities ​ - KPI data for your entities ​ - Cash flow statement data for your entities ​ - Chart of accounts data for your entities |
Forecast and budget data currently cannot be accessed via Fathom's MCP server.
---
# How to connect to Fathom's MCP server
You can connect your AI tool to Fathom’s MCP server with a Personal Access Token (PAT). The PAT will provide your AI tool with read-only access to your data in Fathom.
Because PATs are specific to the individual, your PAT will be able to read data according to your personal role and permissions in Fathom. You cannot access additional data in Fathom with your PAT.
📝 **Note:** OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini do not support PAT connection, so it is currently not possible to connect them to Fathom's MCP server.

*I use a tool called Fathom to track and analyse financial data. I want to give [AI tool’s name] access to my data in Fathom via Fathom’s MCP server. Fathom provides me with a Personal Access Token (PAT) to access the Fathom MCP server. The URL to connect to Fathom’s MCP server is [https://api.fathom.dev/mcp](https://api.fathom.dev/mcp).

mcp.title: GitHub - Dot-Fun/fathom-mcp: Model Context Protocol server for Fathom AI - access meeting recordings, transcripts, summaries, teams, and webhooks
mcp.snippet:
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server for interacting with the [Fathom AI API](https://developers.fathom.ai). This server provides tools for accessing meeting recordings, summaries, transcripts, teams, and webhooks.
## Quick Start
```
git clone https://github.com/Dot-Fun/fathom-mcp.git
cd fathom-mcp
uv pip install fastmcp httpx pydantic
export FATHOM_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
fastmcp run server.py
```
## Features
### Tools
- **list_meetings**: List meetings with advanced filtering (by participants, date ranges, teams) and optional inclusion of transcripts, summaries, action items, and CRM matches
- **get_summary**: Retrieve meeting summaries (supports async delivery)
- **get_transcript**: Retrieve meeting transcripts with speaker information and timestamps (supports async delivery)
- **list_teams**: List all accessible teams
- **list_team_members**: List team members with optional team filtering
- **create_webhook**: Create webhooks for meeting notifications with customizable triggers and content inclusion
- **delete_webhook**: Delete webhooks by ID
### Resources
- **fathom://api/info**: API information and available endpoints
- **fathom://api/rate-limits**: Rate limiting information and best practices

### Running the Server
#### Local Development (stdio)
```
# Using fastmcp CLI
fastmcp run server.py
# Or directly with Python
python server.py
```
#### HTTP Server
```
# Modify server.py to run as HTTP server
if __name__ == "__main__":
mcp.run(transport="http", host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

mcp.title: AI Meeting Notetaker MCP Server for Claude & ChatGPT
mcp.snippet:
# It’s your meeting. Bring context into Claude, ChatGPT, and the AI tools you use.
Fathom’s AI meeting notetaker MCP server connects your meeting data to Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP-compatible tools, so your AI assistant can answer questions and draft work from what was actually said.

Stop pasting summaries and transcripts into chat to get context.
Ask your AI assistant about any meeting you can access in Fathom.
Combine meeting context with your docs, plans, and other connected tools.

### Ask your assistant about your meetings.
Ask Claude what a customer pushed back on last week, or have ChatGPT pull the decisions from Monday’s planning call. Your assistant retrieves the context from Fathom directly, so you’re not hunting for the right summary to paste in.

### Turn meeting context into finished work.
Ask Fathom answers questions inside Fathom. MCP brings the same meeting context into the assistant where you’re already drafting, so a recap email, QBR narrative, or launch brief starts from what was said, right alongside your docs and other connected tools.

### Connect in a few steps, on the permissions you already have.
Add the Fathom app in ChatGPT or the Fathom connector in Claude, or point any MCP-compatible tool at Fathom’s MCP server and sign in. Your assistant can only reach meetings you can already view in Fathom. MCP doesn’t open up any new data.

An AI meeting notetaker MCP server connects your meeting notes to AI assistants using the Model Context Protocol. Fathom’s MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP-compatible tools answer questions and draft work from what was actually said in your meetings.
### Which AI tools work with Fathom MCP?
Fathom MCP works with ChatGPT (through the Fathom app), Claude (through the Fathom connector or Claude Code), and any MCP-compatible tool using the server URL https://api.fathom.ai/mcp.

mcp.snippet:
> **MCP server for Fathom.video** — Access your AI meeting transcripts, summaries, and action items directly from Cursor IDE

A [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that integrates [Fathom.video](https://fathom.video) with AI coding assistants like Cursor. Query your meeting transcripts, export recordings to markdown, search by participant, and manage webhooks — all through natural language.
## Features
- **📋 List & Search Meetings** — Browse recordings with filters for date, team, participants, or external domains
- **📝 Full Transcripts** — Get speaker-labeled, timestamped transcripts formatted as markdown
- **📊 AI Summaries** — Access Fathom's AI-generated meeting summaries
- **✅ Action Items** — Pull action items from specific meetings or across recent calls
- **📁 Export to Markdown** — Save meetings as `MeetingTitle_YYYY-MM-DD.md` files
- **👥 Team Management** — List teams and team members
- **🔔 Webhooks** — Create and manage webhooks for real-time notifications
## Quick Start
### 1. Get Your Fathom API Key
1. Go to [Fathom Settings](https://fathom.video/settings)
2. Navigate to **API Access**
3. Click **Generate API Key**
### 2. Install the MCP Server
```
git clone https://github.com/matthewbergvinson/fathom-mcp.git
cd fathom-mcp
npm install
npm run build
```
### 3. Configure Cursor
Add to your `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"fathom": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/path/to/fathom-mcp/dist/index.js"],
"env": {
"FATHOM_API_KEY": "your-api-key-here",
"FATHOM_OUTPUT_DIR": "/path/to/export/transcripts"
}
}
}
}
```
> **Note:** Replace `/path/to/fathom-mcp` with the actual path where you cloned the repo, and add your Fathom API key.
